findings.title: Data skew in stage 1
findings.message: In stage 1 (attempt 0, 'shuffle join') the largest task read 2.52 GiB of shuffle read data vs a median of 61.10 MiB (42.2x). The slowest task took 52.3 s vs 3.1 s median, so up to 49.3 s of stage time is spent waiting on it.
findings.recommendation: Enable Adaptive Query Execution skew-join handling (spark.sql.adaptive.enabled and spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled), salt hot keys, pre-aggregate before the shuffle, or broadcast the smaller side of the join.

findings.title: High garbage-collection time in stage 2
findings.message: JVM GC consumed 25.0% of executor run time in stage 2 (attempt 0, 'sessionize') (5m 31s of 22m 05s).
findings.recommendation: Give executors more memory or fewer cores, prefer the built-in DataFrame API over RDD/UDF object-heavy code, use Kryo serialization, and consider G1GC (-XX:+UseG1GC).

findings.title: Job 6 failed
findings.message: Job aborted due to stage failure: Task 3 in stage 7.0 failed 4 times, most recent failure: java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero

evidence.reason: Job aborted due to stage failure: Task 3 in stage 7.0 failed 4 times, most recent failure: java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero

findings.recommendation: Inspect the failing stage's task errors and executor logs; fix the root cause before tuning.

findings.title: Stage 4 cannot use the whole cluster
findings.message: stage 4 (attempt 0, 'single partition sort') ran only 1 task(s) for 5m 30s while up to 32 cores were available.
findings.recommendation: Increase partitions (repartition, spark.sql.shuffle.partitions, spark.default.parallelism), avoid single-partition operations such as global sorts or coalesce(1), and split large non-splittable files.

findings.title: Out-of-memory or container memory-limit kills detected
findings.message: 14 memory-related failure event(s), e.g. ExecutorLostFailure: Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits. 8.4 GB of 8 GB physical memory used. Consider boosting spark.exe…; Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits. 8.4 GB of 8 GB physical memory used. Consider boosting spark.executor.memoryOverhead.

Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits. 8.4 GB of 8 GB physical memory used. Consider boosting spark.executor.memoryOverhead.

findings.recommendation: Raise spark.executor.memory and/or spark.executor.memoryOverhead (YARN/K8s kills usually mean off-heap overhead is too small), reduce partition size (more partitions), avoid collecting large results, and check for skewed keys.

findings.title: 12 failed task(s) in stage 5
findings.message: 9.7% of tasks in stage 5 (attempt 0, 'extract features') failed. Most common: ExecutorLostFailure: Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits. 8.4 GB of 8 GB physical memory used. Consider boosting spark.exec… (x12)

findings.recommendation: Failed attempts re-run work. Review the top failure reasons; if they are transient (executor loss, fetch failures) address cluster stability, otherwise fix the code/data issue.

findings.recommendation: Failed attempts re-run work. Review the top failure reasons; if they are transient (executor loss, fetch failures) address cluster stability, otherwise fix the code/data issue.

findings.title: Spill to disk in stage 1
findings.message: stage 1 (attempt 0, 'shuffle join') spilled 2.05 GiB to disk (9.00 GiB in-memory size). Spilling means execution memory was too small for the working set and adds heavy disk I/O.
findings.recommendation: Increase the number of shuffle partitions (smaller tasks), raise spark.executor.memory or spark.memory.fraction, reduce executor cores per executor, or filter/aggregate earlier.

findings.title: 2 executor(s) were lost unexpectedly
findings.message: Executors disappeared for reasons other than a normal scale-down: Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits. 8.4 GB of 8 GB physical memory used. Consider boosting spark.exec… (x2)

reasons.reason: Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits. 8.4 GB of 8 GB physical memory used. Consider boosting spark.exec…

findings.recommendation: Look for OOM kills, node preemption/spot reclamation, or failing disks. Cached data and shuffle output on lost executors must be recomputed.

findings.title: High garbage-collection time in stage 4
findings.message: JVM GC consumed 13.6% of executor run time in stage 4 (attempt 0, 'single partition sort') (45.0 s of 5m 30s).
findings.recommendation: Give executors more memory or fewer cores, prefer the built-in DataFrame API over RDD/UDF object-heavy code, use Kryo serialization, and consider G1GC (-XX:+UseG1GC).

findings.title: Large result returned to the driver in stage 4
findings.message: stage 4 (attempt 0, 'single partition sort') sent 1.50 GiB of task results to the driver (collect/toPandas/take?).
findings.recommendation: Write results to storage instead of collecting them; if collecting is required, aggregate or limit first and size spark.driver.memory / spark.driver.maxResultSize accordingly.

findings.title: Cluster cores were mostly idle
findings.message: Tasks kept only 24.2% of the 4h 53m of provisioned core-time busy (dynamic allocation disabled).
findings.recommendation: Right-size the cluster or enable dynamic allocation (spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled=true with shuffle tracking) so executors are released while the driver or a single-threaded stage is working.

findings.title: Scheduler / launch overhead in stage 3
findings.message: About 38.2% of task wall time in stage 3 (attempt 0, 'scan many small files') is not spent running, deserializing or serializing (scheduler delay, result fetch, launch latency).
findings.recommendation: Use fewer, larger tasks, check driver CPU/GC and network latency between driver and executors, and avoid very large task results.

findings.title: Task deserialization overhead in stage 2
findings.message: 21.4% of task time in stage 2 (attempt 0, 'sessionize') is spent deserializing the task closure (6m 00s).
findings.recommendation: Large closures are shipped with every task: broadcast big lookup objects, avoid capturing large driver-side collections, and use fewer, larger tasks.

findings.title: Too many tiny tasks in stage 3
findings.message: stage 3 (attempt 0, 'scan many small files') ran 4,000 tasks with a median duration of 58 ms. Task scheduling and serialization overhead likely dominates useful work.
findings.recommendation: Reduce partition counts (coalesce, lower spark.sql.shuffle.partitions), enable AQE partition coalescing (spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled), or compact small input files.

findings.title: Stage 7 was retried 1 time(s)
findings.message: Re-running a stage wastes compute and usually follows lost executors or shuffle fetch failures. 10 FetchFailed task(s) were observed.
findings.recommendation: Check for lost executors / node preemption, enable the external shuffle service or shuffle tracking, and consider raising spark.executor.memoryOverhead.

findings.title: Straggler tasks in stage 2
findings.message: In stage 2 (attempt 0, 'sessionize') the slowest task took 1m 14s vs a median of 7.7 s (9.6x) although input sizes are balanced.
findings.recommendation: Enable speculative execution (spark.speculation=true), check the executors/hosts that ran the slowest tasks for noisy neighbours or bad disks, and look at GC time in those tasks.

findings.title: Adaptive Query Execution is disabled
findings.message: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=false. AQE coalesces shuffle partitions, switches join strategies and splits skewed partitions at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Set spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true (default since Spark 3.2).

findings.title: Java serialization used with significant shuffle volume
findings.message: The application shuffled 14.45 GiB using the default JavaSerializer, which is slower and larger than Kryo for RDD workloads.
findings.recommendation: Set spark.serializer=org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer (DataFrame shuffles already use Tungsten and are unaffected).
